knowledge-base.overview: Language-specific guardrails and patterns for SQL. Loaded when agents work on .sql files, database migrations, or query optimization tasks. Applies to PostgreSQL 15+ and MySQL 8+.

core-principles.principle: Never concatenate user input into SQL strings. Use bind parameters ($1, ?, :name) without exception.
Name all constraints, specify column lists in INSERT, avoid SELECT * in production code.
Once applied to a shared environment, never modify a migration — create a new one.
Every index speeds reads but slows writes; justify each index with a query plan.
Keep transactions short, choose the correct isolation level, and always handle rollback.

guardrail.rule: Always use parameterized queries — never string interpolation of user input.
guardrail.bad: -- BAD: SQL injection vector SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" + userInput + "';
guardrail.good: -- GOOD: parameterized, explicit columns, bounded SELECT u.id, u.email, u.created_at FROM users u WHERE u.email = $1 AND u.is_active = true LIMIT 1;

guardrail.rule: Never use SELECT * in application code. Always specify column lists in INSERT statements.
Always add LIMIT to queries that return lists. Prevent unbounded result sets.
Never use TRUNCATE or DROP in application code without explicit safeguards.
Use EXISTS instead of COUNT(*) > 0 for existence checks. Always qualify column names with table aliases in JOINs.
Migrations must have both up and down. Must be idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS guards). Never modify a migration that has been applied to a shared environment.
Keep transactions as short as possible. No I/O or external calls inside a transaction. Always explicitly COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
Use CONCURRENTLY for index creation on live tables (PostgreSQL). Never create indexes without a query plan justification.

naming-conventions.convention: id (integer or UUID depending on project convention)
is_ or has_ prefix: is_active, has_verified_email

schema-design.description: Standard table template with identity PK, timestamps, and auto-update trigger.

rules.rule: Use BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY for auto-increment PKs (PostgreSQL 10+)
Use UUID PKs when IDs are exposed externally or distributed systems require it
Use TIMESTAMPTZ (not TIMESTAMP) for all time columns — always store UTC
Add NOT NULL constraints by default; allow NULL only when semantically meaningful
Use CHECK constraints to enforce domain rules at the database level
Use ENUM types sparingly — prefer VARCHAR with CHECK for easier migration
Add ON DELETE CASCADE or ON DELETE SET NULL explicitly to every foreign key
Use soft deletes (deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ) when audit trail is required

pattern.name: Common Table Expressions (CTEs)
pattern.description: Prefer CTEs over subqueries for readability and maintainability.
pattern.example: WITH active_orders AS ( SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total_cents) AS total_spent FROM orders WHERE status != 'cancelled' AND created_at >= now() - INTERVAL '30 days' GROUP BY user_id ), high_value_users AS ( SELECT user_id FROM active_orders WHERE total_spent > 50000 ) SELECT u.id, u.email, ao.order_count, ao.total_spent FROM users u JOIN active_orders ao ON ao.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id IN (SELECT user_id FROM high_value_users) ORDER BY ao.total_spent DESC;

pattern.name: Window Functions
pattern.description: Use for ranking, running totals, and row comparisons without self-joins.
pattern.example:
-- Rank users by spending within each region SELECT u.id, u.region, SUM(o.total_cents) AS total_spent, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY u.region ORDER BY SUM(o.total_cents) DESC) AS rank FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.region;
-- Running total of daily revenue SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day, SUM(total_cents) AS daily_revenue, SUM(SUM(total_cents)) OVER (ORDER BY date_trunc('day', created_at)) AS running_total FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' GROUP BY date_trunc('day', created_at) ORDER BY day;

pattern.name: UPSERT
pattern.example: INSERT INTO user_preferences (user_id, theme, language) VALUES ($1, $2, $3) ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET theme = EXCLUDED.theme, language = EXCLUDED.language, updated_at = now();

pattern.name: Batch Operations
pattern.example:
-- Batch insert with unnest (PostgreSQL) INSERT INTO tags (name, category) SELECT unnest($1::text[]), unnest($2::text[]) ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING;
-- Batch update with VALUES list UPDATE products AS p SET price_cents = v.new_price FROM (VALUES (1, 2999), (2, 4999), (3, 1499) ) AS v(id, new_price) WHERE p.id = v.id;

pattern.name: Parameterized Queries — Application Code
N+1 Prevention
pattern.example:
-- GOOD: single query with JOIN SELECT u.id, u.email, o.id AS order_id, o.total_cents FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.is_active = true ORDER BY u.id, o.created_at DESC;
-- GOOD: batch with ANY (when you have a list of IDs) SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[]);

pattern.name: Pagination
pattern.example:
-- Cursor-based pagination (preferred for large datasets) SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users WHERE created_at < $1 AND is_active = true ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 25;
-- Offset-based pagination (simpler but slower for deep pages) SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users WHERE is_active = true ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 25 OFFSET $1;

performance.explain-analyze: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT) SELECT u.id, u.email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.created_at >= '2025-01-01' GROUP BY u.id, u.email ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 20;

what-to-look-for.item: Seq Scan on large tables — usually needs an index
Nested Loop with large outer sets — consider Hash Join via index or rewrite
Sort operations with high cost — add index matching ORDER BY
Rows Removed by Filter much larger than Actual Rows — index the filter column
Buffers: shared hit vs shared read — high reads indicate cold cache

# PostgreSQL CLI psql -h localhost -U myuser -d mydb # Connect psql -f migration.sql mydb # Run migration file pg_dump -Fc mydb > backup.dump # Backup (custom format) pg_restore -d mydb backup.dump # Restore
# Schema inspection \dt # List tables \d+ table_name # Describe table with details \di # List indexes \df # List functions
# Migration tools migrate create -ext sql -dir db/migrations -seq add_users_phone migrate -path db/migrations -database "$DATABASE_URL" up alembic revision -m "add users phone" && alembic upgrade head npx prisma migrate dev --name add_users_phone dbmate new add_users_phone && dbmate up

quick-reference.item: ALWAYS — never string-concat user input into SQL
NEVER in application code — specify columns explicitly
Add to all list queries without exception
Immutable once applied to shared env; always include down
Short, explicit COMMIT/ROLLBACK, correct isolation level
Justify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE; use CONCURRENTLY on live tables
BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (or UUID for external/distributed)
Prefer over nested subqueries for readability
Use JOIN or ANY($1::bigint[]) batch queries
